sourcedFrom: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: One book covers the 1100 and the 11-87, and the two are not the same gun — every procedure below is taken from a section headed Model 1100, because the gas systems, the barrels and the piston stacks differ. On an 1100 the routine clean is barrel off and the piston stack off the magazine tube; the deeper strip that takes the action bars, breech bolt and trigger plate out is the Deep Clean branch.

steps.title: Cross-bolt safety in, red band out of sight
steps.action: Push the safety button behind the trigger until the RED BAND MARKING cannot be seen, and keep your finger outside the guard while you do it.
steps.prose: The 1100's safety is a cross-bolt button through the rear of the trigger guard and it reads by colour, not by feel — a band of red showing on one side means the gun will fire. Push it from the side that makes the red disappear and check by eye rather than by thumb, because a button pushed only part way can still show a sliver. Remington's own instruction is that the safety is engaged whenever the gun is loaded and you do not intend to shoot.
steps.quote: The safety mechanism on the Model 1100/11-87 Shotguns is a button located behind the trigger. See Pictures 3 and 4.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — Important Parts of the Firearm — The Safety Mechanism, p.7
steps.warn: Remington: the firearm will fire when the trigger is pulled and the RED BAND IS SHOWING.

steps.title: An 11-87 barrel is not an 1100 barrel — check what is on the gun
steps.action: Before you take anything off, read the model marking on the receiver and on the barrel and confirm you have an 1100 barrel on an 1100 receiver.
steps.prose: Remington prints this prohibition five separate times in one 26-page book, which tells you how often it gets ignored: the two models' barrels look interchangeable on the magazine tube and are not, because the gas port location and the barrel extension are matched to different gas systems. A mismatched pair either will not cycle or will cycle at a pressure the parts were not designed for. This matters at cleaning time as well as at buying time — a mixed-up pair of barrels in a gun cabinet is exactly how a wrong barrel ends up back on the wrong receiver at reassembly.
steps.caution: This guide is written from the sections headed Model 1100. If the receiver marking says 11-87, you are on the wrong procedure.
steps.quote: WARNING: MODEL 11-87™ BARRELS CAN NOT BE USED AS REPLACEMENT BARRELS ON MODEL 1100 FIREARMS. MODEL 1100 BARRELS CAN NOT BE USED AS REPLACEMENT BARRELS ON MODEL 11-87 FIREARMS.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — To Assemble (Model 1100™) — warning under the heading, p.10

steps.title: And a receiver marked 11-87 Super Magnum is a third gun again
steps.action: If the receiver marking reads MODEL 11-87 SUPER MAGNUM, stop — that gun takes only 3 1⁄2" chambered 12-gauge 11-87 barrels and has its own barrel seal activator, and none of the 1100 procedure applies to it.
steps.prose: The book carries all three guns, so this restriction sits on the same pages as the 1100 material and is easy to read past. The Super Magnum is the one variant that also drops the gas cylinder collar and adds a barrel seal activator to the piston stack, so its strip genuinely differs part for part. Read the receiver, not the box the gun came in — this is the identification the manual asks the owner to make and no model name in a catalogue can make it for you.
steps.quote: MODEL 11-87 SUPER MAGNUM BARREL REPLACEMENT: ONLY MODEL 11-87 12-GAUGE BARRELS HAVING 3 1⁄2" CHAMBERS CAN BE USED ON MODEL 11-87 SUPER MAGNUM RECEIVERS.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — Important Parts of the Firearm — barrel replacement notice, p.9

steps.title: Operating handle back until the carrier latch holds the bolt open
steps.action: Point the gun in a safe direction, safety engaged, and pull the operating handle fully rearward until the bolt is caught and held open by the carrier latch. Then check the chamber and the magazine.
steps.prose: On an 1100 the bolt only stays back if the carrier latch has caught it, so pull the handle all the way to its stop rather than most of the way — a bolt that runs forward again while you have your fingers in the port is the injury this step exists to prevent. With it locked open, look into the ejection port for the chamber and then push a finger up into the magazine tube through the loading port; a shell held by the shell latch does not show itself from the top. Two shells is a full check on this gun: the one in the chamber and whatever the tube is holding.
steps.quote: 3. Pull the operating handle fully rearward until the bolt is held open by the carrier latch.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — To Disassemble (Model 1100™), step 3, p.14
steps.warn: Remington opens the disassembly with it: check the chamber and the magazine to make sure there are no shells in the firearm.

steps.title: Magazine cap off, fore-end forward, barrel out of the receiver
steps.action: Unscrew and remove the magazine cap, slide the fore-end forward off the magazine tube, then hold the barrel ahead of the gas cylinder and pull it straight out of the receiver.
steps.prose: Take hold of the barrel at the gas cylinder, not at the muzzle — the gas cylinder is the part that has to come off the magazine tube and levering from the muzzle cocks it in the tube. The barrel comes away without force once the cap is off; if it does not, the fore-end is still on the tube or the bolt is not held back. Keep the gas cylinder from grinding down the tube on the way off, because the carbon on a fired 1100's magazine tube is abrasive and the tube's finish is what the action bar sleeve rides on.
steps.quote: 4. Unscrew and remove the magazine cap. 5. Slide the fore-end forward and remove it from the magazine tube. 6. Hold the barrel in front of the gas cylinder. Pull the barrel from the receiver.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — To Disassemble (Model 1100™), steps 4-6, p.14

steps.title: Barrel seal, piston and piston seal off the magazine tube
steps.action: Slide the barrel seal, the piston and the piston seal off the front of the magazine tube, keeping them in the order they come off.
steps.prose: This stack is the whole reason a gas gun needs cleaning more often than a pump: the piston and seal live in the gas stream and carbon them up until the action starts short-stroking. The parts are not symmetrical and they do not go back in any order that fits — note which face of each pointed at the muzzle as it comes off, and lay them out in a line on the bench rather than dropping them in a tray. The rubber barrel seal is the fragile one; if it has gone hard or has taken a set, that is a part to replace rather than to scrub.
steps.caution: The 1100 procedure has no gas cylinder collar step and no barrel seal activator. Those belong to 11-87 variants — do not go looking for parts your gun does not have.
steps.quote: 7. Slide the barrel seal, piston and piston seal from the magazine tube. See Picture 20.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — To Disassemble (Model 1100™), step 7, p.14

steps.title: Which piston parts you are holding depends on the gauge
steps.action: Check the gauge marking on the barrel: a 12-gauge 1100 carries a piston/piston seal assembly, while an 1100 in 20, 28 or .410 carries a separate piston and piston seal.
steps.prose: The book keeps the two apart because they are cleaned the same way but counted differently, and a small-gauge owner who is looking for a one-piece assembly will conclude a part is missing. Both get scrubbed with steel wool and cleaning solvent and wiped clean and dry — this is the one place on the gun where Remington actually calls for steel wool, because carbon on a gas piston is baked on rather than merely dirty. Do not oil them afterwards: an oiled piston collects the next lot of carbon and glues itself into the cylinder.
steps.aside: The same list names the alternative directly underneath: the separate piston and piston seal used on the Model 1100 in 20, 28 and .410 gauge.
steps.quote: THE PISTON/PISTON SEAL ASSEMBLY: (USED ON MODEL 11-87 12-GA., 11-87 SUPER MAGNUM™ AND MODEL 1100™ 12-GA.)
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — Lubrication and Maintenance — component list, p.16

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Barrel off, fore-end off, barrel seal and piston stack off the magazine tube, chamber and magazine empty. That is the 1100 field strip — receiver, bolt, action bars and trigger plate all stay in the gun.
steps.prose: That gets you the bore, the chamber, the barrel's locking notch, the gas hole in the gas cylinder and the whole outside of the magazine tube, which is where a gas gun's problems actually live. Going further — operating handle out, action bar assembly and breech bolt out, trigger plate pins driven and the trigger plate assembly out of the bottom of the receiver — is the deeper procedure the book prints on page 14, and it is what the Deep Clean branch walks.
steps.quote: The Model 11-87™ Autoloading Shotgun and Model 1100™ Autoloading Shotgun are gas-operated firearms. Gas operation provides significant recoil reduction by bleeding gases off the barrel to pressurize a piston which unlocks and functions the action.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — Lubrication and Maintenance — CLEANING, p.16

deepSteps.title: Close the action on the handle, then pull the handle out of the bolt
deepSteps.action: Hold the operating handle and let the action close, then pull the operating handle straight out of the breech bolt.
deepSteps.prose: The handle is a push-fit stud into the side of the bolt and it only clears the ejection port at one point in the bolt's travel, which is why the action closes first — trying to pull it with the bolt locked back just bends your fingers around it. Control the closing rather than letting the action springs slam it; the bolt is running forward onto an empty chamber and there is nothing to stop it but the barrel extension, which is not in the gun. Once out, the handle is loose and small: pocket it or it will end up on the floor.
deepSteps.quote: 8. Hold the operating handle and close the action. 9. Pull the operating handle from the bolt. See Picture 21.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — To Disassemble (Model 1100™), steps 8-9, p.14

deepSteps.title: Carrier up, feed latch held, action bar assembly forward off the tube
deepSteps.action: Push the carrier release and lift the carrier, reach into the bottom of the receiver and press and hold the feed latch, then draw the action bar assembly out of the receiver and off the magazine tube and release the latch.
deepSteps.prose: The feed latch is the sprung tab inside the bottom left of the receiver, and until it is held down it stands in the path of the action bar sleeve — this is the step people force, and forcing it bends the latch and gives you a gun that will not feed. Hold it flat with a fingertip and the whole assembly slides forward off the tube with no resistance at all. Keep the assembly square as it comes off so the two action bars do not spring apart at the sleeve.
deepSteps.quote: 10. Push the carrier release and push upward on the carrier. 11. Reach in the bottom of the receiver. Press and hold the feed latch. See Picture 22. 12. Pull the action bar assembly from the receiver and the magazine tube. Release the feed latch.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — To Disassemble (Model 1100™), steps 10-12, p.14

deepSteps.title: Breech bolt off the rear of the action bar assembly
deepSteps.action: Lift the breech bolt assembly off the rear of the action bar assembly.
deepSteps.prose: The bolt sits on a block at the back of the action bars and is only located there, not latched, so once the assembly is out of the receiver the bolt lifts straight off. Watch the locking block underneath it — on an 1100 the locking block cams down out of the barrel extension and it is loose enough to shift as you handle the bolt. Keep the bolt and its locking block together as a pair; the locking block is fitted and is not a part to mix between guns.
deepSteps.quote: 13. Lift the breech bolt assembly from the rear of the action bar assembly.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — To Disassemble (Model 1100™), step 13, p.14

deepSteps.title: Both trigger plate pins out, trigger plate rearward and down
deepSteps.action: Tap out the front and rear trigger plate pins, then lift the rear of the trigger plate assembly, slide it rearward and take it out of the bottom of the receiver.
deepSteps.prose: The pins are a light push fit and go out with a punch and gentle taps — if a pin needs real force, the trigger plate is under load and needs supporting, not hitting harder. The plate has to move rearward before it will drop, because the carrier pivot at its front is captured in the receiver. Keep the two pins identified: the front and rear are not always the same length, and swapping them can leave one proud enough to foul the fore-end.
deepSteps.quote: 14. Tap out the front and rear trigger plate pins. See Picture 25 on page 15. 15. Lift the rear of the trigger plate assembly, slide rearward and remove it from the receiver.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — To Disassemble (Model 1100™), steps 14-15, p.14

deepSteps.title: Keep the safety on so the hammer cannot fall
deepSteps.action: Leave the safety engaged, red band hidden, through the whole trigger plate removal — the hammer must not be allowed to snap forward once the plate is out of the receiver.
deepSteps.prose: Out of the gun the trigger plate is a live spring-loaded assembly, and a hammer that falls with nothing in front of it hammers the sear and the hammer face against each other. Remington's own remedy is exactly the safety button you already set: with the safety in, the trigger cannot be pulled and the hammer cannot be released by accident while you are handling the plate. Set the plate down hammer-side up so nothing on the bench can press the trigger.
deepSteps.quote: WARNING: DO NOT allow the hammer to snap forward when the trigger plate assembly is removed. This can best be assured by keeping the safety mechanism engaged at all times. RED BAND WILL NOT SHOW.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — To Disassemble (Model 1100™) — warning after step 15, p.14

deepSteps.title: Trigger plate assembly: oil only, and as one unit
deepSteps.action: Do not take the trigger plate apart. Spray it with Rem Oil as the manual's Picture 28 shows, let it stand for fifteen minutes, spray it again to wash the components off, and shake the excess out.
deepSteps.prose: This is a wash, not a lubrication — the second spray is there to flush out what the first one loosened, which is why the fifteen-minute soak matters and why the excess is shaken off rather than left in. Solvent is deliberately not used here; the assembly holds small springs and a plastic carrier dog follower that a harsh cleaner can attack. Shake it out thoroughly, because oil pooled in the trigger plate runs down into the stock head and softens the wood over time.
deepSteps.quote: Spray the trigger plate assembly with Rem™ Oil as shown. See Picture 28. Let stand for 15 minutes. Spray again to wash off components. Shake off excess lubricant.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — Lubrication and Maintenance — THE TRIGGER PLATE ASSEMBLY, p.17
deepSteps.warn: Remington: excessive use of a non-recommended lubricant could cause serious function problems possibly leading to accidental firing.

deepSteps.title: Receiver inside, magazine tube outside
deepSteps.action: Brush the inside of the receiver with cleaning solvent and wipe it dry, then clean the outside surface of the magazine tube with solvent and wipe it dry with a clean cloth.
deepSteps.prose: The magazine tube's outside is the surface the action bar sleeve slides on for every shot, and carbon there is the most common cause of an 1100 that short-strokes — it is worth more attention than the inside of the receiver. Wipe it dry rather than oiling it; a light film is enough and heavy oil on the tube collects grit and does the same job as the carbon you just removed. Watch your hands inside the receiver: there are sharp edges around the ejection port on these guns.
deepSteps.quote: 1. Brush the inside of the receiver with cleaning solvent and wipe dry. 2. Clean the outside surface of the magazine tube with cleaning solvent, then wipe dry with a clean cloth.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — Lubrication and Maintenance — THE RECEIVER ASSEMBLY, p.17

deepSteps.title: Clear the gas hole in the gas cylinder with a wire
deepSteps.action: With the barrel off, check the gas hole in the gas cylinder and clean it with a 1/16" diameter wire.
deepSteps.prose: That single small port is what drives the entire action, and a partly carboned hole shows up as an intermittent failure to eject long before it shows up as a gun that will not run at all. Push the wire through and back rather than scraping around the mouth of the hole, and never open it out with a drill — its diameter is the gun's gas regulation. While the barrel is off, take the shooting residue out of the locking notch in the barrel extension at the same time; that notch is what the locking block engages.
deepSteps.quote: 8. Check the gas hole in the gas cylinder. Use a 1/16" diameter wire to clean the gas hole. See Picture 27.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — Lubrication and Maintenance — TO CLEAN THE BARREL, step 8, p.16
deepSteps.warn: Remington: after cleaning, make sure the barrel is free of obstructions.

cleaning.name: BARREL, CHOKE & GAS HOLE
tasks: Correct-gauge brush wet with solvent through the bore several times, then patches until one comes out clean
Take every trace of shooting residue out of the locking notch in the barrel
Check and clear the gas hole in the gas cylinder with a 1/16" wire
Choke tube out, threads and body cleaned with solvent, wiped dry, oil on the threads before it goes back
Never fire the gun without a choke tube properly installed

cleaning.name: GAS PARTS & MAGAZINE TUBE
tasks: 12-gauge: piston/piston seal assembly. 20, 28 and .410: separate piston and piston seal
Scrub the piston parts with steel wool and cleaning solvent, then wipe clean and DRY — no oil on a gas piston
Barrel seal wiped clean; replace it rather than scrub it if it has hardened or taken a set
Outside of the magazine tube cleaned with solvent and wiped dry — this is the surface the action bar sleeve rides
Action bars, with the action bar sleeve attached, brushed with solvent and wiped clean and dry

cleaning.name: BOLT, RECEIVER & TRIGGER PLATE (deep only)
tasks: Breech bolt brushed with cleaning solvent and wiped clean and dry
Inside of the receiver brushed with solvent and wiped dry
Trigger plate assembly washed with Rem Oil as a unit — sprayed, stood 15 minutes, sprayed again, excess shaken off
Never disassemble the trigger plate assembly
Thin coat of oil on external surfaces only; over-lubrication is what fouls a gas gun in cold damp weather

reassembly: Check the inside of the receiver first and make sure the link is in position.
Trigger plate: confirm the end of the disconnector is below the end of the left connector, then insert the plate carrier-first, align the holes and tap in the front and rear trigger plate pins.
Remove the magazine cap, slide the action bar sleeve over the magazine tube, and place the breech bolt assembly on the block at the rear of the action bar assembly.
Slide the action bar assembly in until the feed latch stops it, push the carrier release and lift the carrier, then press and hold the feed latch and slide the assembly the rest of the way in.
Push the operating handle into the breech bolt.

Model 1100 12-gauge: slide the piston/piston seal assembly and barrel seal over the magazine tube. Model 1100 in 20, 28 and .410: piston seal, piston and barrel seal, in that order and in the position the manual's Picture 33b shows.
Operating handle fully rearward to open the action, then replace the barrel, slide the fore-end over the magazine tube, and replace and tighten the magazine cap.
Chamber and bore wiped thoroughly dry before the gun is used or stored.
fncheck: With chamber and magazine confirmed empty: the operating handle pulled fully rearward should be caught and held by the carrier latch, and the bolt should run fully forward and lock when released. The safety button should travel fully both ways and show the red band on one side only — with the band hidden the trigger must not move the hammer. Work the carrier up and down by hand and confirm the feed latch and shell latch return under their own springs. Finally check the choke tube is present and tight; Remington's instruction is never to fire the gun without one installed.
